author: a. w. anderson
title: Joe Sheridan named Richmond's Atlantic 10 postgraduate scholarship recipient
text:
University of Richmond midfielder Joe Sheridan was named the university’s recipient of the Atlantic 10’s postgraduate scholarship, according to a May 27 announcement. The scholarship is awarded annually to one student-athlete from each of the 14 member institutions in the Atlantic 10 Conference.
Sheridan joins a group consisting of six female and eight male student-athletes representing seven different sports, and he is the only men’s lacrosse player among this year’s honorees. The group achieved an average GPA of 3.816, which matches the highest mark since the program expanded to include 14 recipients.
The Atlantic 10 Postgraduate Scholarship provides financial support for student-athletes pursuing advanced academic or professional degrees after graduation. Sheridan plans to use his award toward medical school. Eligibility for the scholarship requires distinction in both academics and athletics, as well as exemplary character and leadership within their communities.
Sheridan, a Biochemistry and Molecular Biology major with a 3.9 GPA, helped lead Richmond men’s lacrosse to one of its most successful seasons in program history in 2026. He was named Atlantic 10 Midfielder of the Year, earned a spot on the All-Academic Team, and was recognized as an All-American during this period.
Over the past decade, more than $612,000 has been awarded through this program to support former student-athletes’ postgraduate studies. Currently, $42,000 is distributed annually across conference schools for full-time study at graduate or professional programs. A-10 Commissioner Dan Leibovitz said, “I would like to congratulate our outstanding group of student-athletes. Each recipient of our Postgraduate Scholarship has demonstrated excellence both in competition and in the classroom. As part of our ongoing commitment to supporting student-athletes, the Atlantic 10 is proud to assist with their postgraduate studies. We look forward to following the future successes of these 14 deserving honorees.”
